name: Hurricanes and post-tropical storms – Atlantic Canada and eastern Quebec

geo.extent: Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland, New Brunswick and eastern Quebec coasts

description: Late-summer and autumn tropical systems reach Atlantic Canada. Fiona (24 September 2022) hit eastern Nova Scotia with sustained winds of 165 km/h and 932.7 hPa, the deepest pressure recorded over land in Canada; gusts over 100 km/h in five provinces, more than 600,000 customers without power, three deaths and $846 million in insured losses (to the date of the ECCC report).

exposed_areas: Cape Breton and eastern Nova Scotia
practical_implications: Storm surge, coastal erosion and long power outages
Coastal setbacks and insurance for waterfront property
Coastal flooding is expected to increase with local sea-level rise (CCCR 2019)

sources.title: Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: PEI erosion-rate data from the provincial site could not be fetched (blocked twice on 2026-10-30). Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
